questions.stem: A plant cell placed in pure water becomes firm and swollen. Why does it not burst?

options.text: The cell membrane is strong enough to resist the pressure
The cell wall provides support and prevents the cell from bursting
Water stops entering the cell once the vacuole is full
The nucleus controls how much water can enter

questions.explanation: When water enters a plant cell by osmosis, the cell swells and becomes turgid. The rigid cell wall resists further expansion and prevents the cell from bursting, unlike animal cells which lack a cell wall and can lyse in pure water.
